description: Adds a UK train booking to the person’s Untap account and works out Delay Repay for it. One booking per call, with each journey in legs (one for a single, two for a return, in travel order). Untap checks National Rail’s Historical Service Performance records for each journey; the delay, actual arrival and cancellation fields are optional, and when left out Untap looks them up. Operators accept one journey per claim form, so a return with both directions late means two claims. A train journey that is already saved is returned as it is, not saved twice. Requires sign-in to Untap.

booking_reference.description: Booking reference if available, otherwise null.

legs.description: Each journey on this booking, in travel order: one for a single, two for a return (outward first), more for a multi-stop booking. Untap works out Delay Repay for each journey and adds them up.

actual_arrival.description: Optional. Actual arrival for this journey as an ISO 8601 datetime, if known. When left out, Untap looks it up.

arrival_station.description: Full arrival station name, e.g. "Edinburgh Waverley".

delay_minutes.description: Optional. Delay at arrival for this journey, in minutes, if known. When left out, Untap looks it up in National Rail records.

departure_station.description: Full departure station name, e.g. "London Kings Cross".

operator_toc_code.description: National Rail two-letter operator code for this journey: VT=Avanti West Coast, CC=c2c, CH=Chiltern Railways, EM=East Midlands Railway, GX=Gatwick Express, GN=Great Northern, GW=Great Western Railway, LE=Greater Anglia, NT=Northern Trains, SW=South Western Railway, SE=Southeastern, SN=Southern, TL=Thameslink, TP=TransPennine Express, AW=Transport for Wales, LM=West Midlands Railway, LN=London Northwestern Railway, XC=CrossCountry, GR=LNER, SR=ScotRail, LD=Lumo, HT=Hull Trains, CS=Caledonian Sleeper

was_cancelled.description: Optional. True when this journey was cancelled. When set, no National Rail lookup is made.

ticket_price_pence.description: Total fare paid in pence for the whole booking. £62.00 = 6200.

ticket_type.description: Ticket type as printed. For "return" and "open_return" the single fare is half the price paid; every other type uses the full price as the single fare.

name: add_train_journey
